1.title: Solomon's request
1.text: God appeared to Solomon by night at Gibeon and said, 'Ask what I shall give thee.' Solomon asked not for riches or long life, but for wisdom and knowledge to govern the people.

1.question: What was at Gibeon, leading Solomon to sacrifice there?
options: The tabernacle of the congregation and the bronze altar
The ark of the covenant with the tablets of the law kept in Jerusalem
The royal palace with cedar pillars later built by David
The temple that Solomon would eventually build

1.question: What did Solomon ask of God at Gibeon?
options: Wisdom and knowledge to govern the people
Riches and honor greater than any other king
Long life and many days of reign over Israel
The death of all his enemies and rivals

1.question: What did God give Solomon beyond what he asked?
options: Riches, wealth, and honor like no king had
Only wisdom, without riches or material wealth
A powerful army to quickly defeat all his enemies
Long life lasting until a very old age

1.question: What marked Solomon's reign according to the chapter's end?
options: Accumulation of chariots, horses, and great wealth
Widespread poverty and lack of resources in the kingdom
Constant war against the neighboring kingdoms of Israel
Exile forced far away from his native land

2.title: A great house
2.text: Solomon said the house would be great, 'for great is our God above all gods.' Even the heavens cannot contain him; the temple would only be a place to burn incense before him.

2.question: Whom did Solomon ask for help in building the temple?
options: Huram, king of Tyre
Pharaoh Shishak, king of Egypt
The king Hadadezer, king of Syria
King Toi, of Hamath

2.question: What did Solomon ask of Huram besides timber?
options: A skilled craftsman to work in gold, silver, and bronze
A great amount of gold to cover the entire temple in Jerusalem
Experienced soldiers to guard the entire border of the kingdom
Ships to carry riches across the whole Mediterranean sea

2.question: Whom did Solomon assign to the heavy labor of the temple?
options: The foreigners dwelling in the land
The Levites in charge of temple services
The free Israelites chosen for the work
Prisoners of war brought by David

3.title: Mount Moriah
3.text: Solomon built the temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, in the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite — the same mount of ancient sacred memory.

3.question: How did Solomon overlay the inside of the temple?
options: He covered it with fine gold and cypress
With finely carved stone of very great value
With pure and fine silver brought from Egypt
With polished bronze on the walls

3.question: What did Solomon make for the most holy place?
options: Two cherubim of carved work, overlaid with gold
An altar of incense overlaid with pure refined gold
A table of showbread made of very fine noble wood
A bronze laver for the priests' washings

3.question: What names did Solomon give the two pillars before the temple?
options: Jachin and Boaz
Jachin and Jachal
Boaz and Obed
Salem and Zion

4.title: The molten sea
4.text: Huram made a great bronze 'sea,' round, resting on twelve oxen — three facing each direction. It was for the priests to wash in.

4.question: On what did the great molten sea rest?
options: Twelve bronze oxen
Cedar pillars
Iron wheels
Silver pillars

4.question: How many golden lampstands did Solomon put in the temple?
options: Ten
One
Seven
Twelve

4.question: Who made the bronze furnishings of the temple?
options: Huram
Solomon
The Levites
David

4.question: Of what material were the finest furnishings of the temple?
options: Pure gold
Silver
Bronze
Iron

5.title: The glory fills the house
5.text: When the musicians and singers praised as one voice — 'for he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever' — a cloud filled the house of the Lord, and the priests could not minister because of God's glory.

5.question: What did the priests and Levites bring into the temple?
options: The ark of the covenant and the holy vessels
The golden throne and the royal crown of David, his father
The silver vessels and the priestly garments of Aaron
The firstfruits and the tithes of all the people

5.question: Where was the ark placed in the temple?
options: In the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim
In the inner court, beside the golden altar of incense
In the treasury chamber, next to the offerings of gold
At the entrance of the tent of meeting for the people

5.question: Why could the priests not minister in the temple?
options: Because the glory of the Lord, as a cloud, filled the house
Because a strong wind knocked down the temple's sacred doors
Because the people refused to enter during the ceremony
Because oil ran out for the lamps of the sanctuary

6.title: There is no God like thee
6.text: Solomon prayed: 'Lord God of Israel, there is no God like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and shewest mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their hearts.'

6.question: What did God say he had not chosen before choosing David?
options: A city or man to be prince over Israel
A temple or an altar to receive the ark of the covenant
A prophet or priest to govern all his people
A sacred mountain to build an altar upon

6.question: Who built the temple, fulfilling the word given to David?
options: Solomon, David's son
Huram, the allied king of Tyre
Zadok, the high priest of Israel
Nathan, the king's prophet

6.question: What did Solomon acknowledge God had fulfilled to David?
options: The promise spoken by his mouth and fulfilled by his hand
A covenant sealed with blood and confirmed by the prophets
A great military victory promised by the angel of the Lord
A blessing promised only to the priests of the temple

6.question: What did Solomon ask God to do when hearing the prayers?
options: To hear from heaven and forgive
That he send angels to protect the people
That he destroy the foreign altars
That he bless the harvests

6.question: What did Solomon ask for when the people sinned and were defeated?
options: That on turning back, God would forgive and bring them home
That even without repenting, God would give them another promised land
That they be given forever into the hands of neighboring foreign nations
That they be taken to serve other gods without return

6.question: Why did Solomon ask God's forgiveness for the people?
options: That they might fear him and walk in his ways
That they might receive riches and multiply their flocks
That they might defeat all the neighboring nations in battle
That they might build more fortified cities

6.question: What did Solomon ask when the people went to war praying toward the temple?
options: That God hear their prayer from heaven and maintain their cause
That he send more chariots and horsemen to defend them from their enemies
That he punish the people severely for their sins before the battle
That he send prophets to proclaim their coming victory

6.question: How did Solomon end his prayer?
options: Asking God to remember the mercies promised to David
Asking that the people soon build a second temple in Jerusalem
Calling the priests to immediately offer new sacrifices
Announcing to the people the end of wars against neighbors

7.title: If my people humble themselves
7.text: God said: 'If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.'

7.question: What happened when Solomon finished praying?
options: Fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices
A thick cloud covered the whole temple of Jerusalem
The king Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar
The priests sang a new song of praise

7.question: How did the Lord appear to Solomon after the feast?
options: By night, saying he had heard his prayer
In a vision before all the people gathered at the temple
Through a formal letter sent by the temple priests
Speaking aloud during the sacrifice

7.question: What did God promise Solomon if he walked like David?
options: To establish his throne over Israel
To send him eternal prosperity
To greatly multiply his seed
To give him fame among the nations

7.question: What would be the reason for ruin, if Israel forsook God?
options: For having left the Lord and served other gods
For having broken the covenant made with Moses in the wilderness
For having built pagan altars inside the sacred temple
For having despised the prophets sent by God

8.title: Care for the holy
8.text: Solomon moved Pharaoh's daughter out of the City of David, saying she should not dwell where the ark had entered, for those places were holy.

8.question: What did Solomon build besides the temple and palace?
options: Cities, including Tadmor in the wilderness
Fortresses along the border with Egypt
A new temple in Jerusalem for the Levites
Naval ports along the coast of Phoenicia

8.question: Whom did Solomon NOT enslave in his work?
options: The children of Israel
The children of the Hittites
The children of the Amorites
The king's captains

8.question: By what did Solomon organize the service of priests and Levites?
options: By the order of David his father
By the custom of Moses
By the counsel of the elders
By the law of the Egyptians

8.question: From where did Solomon and Huram's fleets bring gold?
options: From Ophir
From Syria
From Babylon
From Egypt

9.title: The half was not told me
9.text: The queen of Sheba, seeing Solomon's wisdom and wealth, said she had not believed the reports until she saw with her own eyes — and that not even half had been told her.

9.question: Why did the queen of Sheba come to Solomon?
options: To test him with hard questions
To negotiate a trade treaty with Israel
To ask for her daughter's hand in marriage
To pay homage at the temple of the Lord

9.question: What did Solomon do with the algum wood brought from Ophir?
options: Steps for the temple and palace, and harps and psalteries
Bronze gates for the courtyard of the temple and royal palace
Support pillars for the great throne hall of the king
Weapons and instruments of war for the army

9.question: Of what material was Solomon's great throne?
options: Ivory, overlaid with pure gold
Of cedar wood, overlaid with silver
Of polished bronze, inlaid with precious stones
Of solid gold without ornament

9.question: What did Solomon's fleets bring on their return?
options: Gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks
Wheat, oil, wine, and flocks of sheep
Cedar wood, dyed wool, and fine linens
Horses and chariots from Egypt

9.question: Over which kings did Solomon rule?
options: Over all kings from the Euphrates to Egypt
Over all kings from the Red Sea to Assyria
Over all kings of the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean
Over the neighboring kings of Moab and Ammon

9.question: What happened at the end of Solomon's reign?
options: He died, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place
He became a priest and served in the temple until he died
He divided the kingdom between his two sons before dying
He was deposed by the council of elders

10.title: The rejected counsel
10.text: Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders, who asked him to ease the people's yoke, and followed the counsel of the young men who grew up with him — a decision that split the kingdom.

10.question: What did the people ask of Rehoboam at Shechem?
options: To ease the heavy yoke his father had laid on them
That he would appoint Jeroboam as his chief royal counselor
That he divide the kingdom equally among the tribes
That he forgive all the debts of the people

10.question: What did the young men advise Rehoboam to answer?
options: That he would make the yoke even heavier
That he would call a new council of elders
That he would divide the kingdom into two equal parts
That he would forgive the people's debt

10.question: Why did Rehoboam not heed the people?
options: Because this turn was from God, fulfilling the word to Jeroboam
Because the elders advised him to act harshly toward the people
Because he had sworn never to yield to a rebellious people's demands
Because he feared losing the support of the young men at court

10.question: What was the result of Rehoboam's harsh answer?
options: Israel (the ten tribes) rebelled against the house of David
The elders of Israel united to depose Rehoboam from the throne
The people accepted the heavy yoke and began paying double tribute
Jeroboam was captured and expelled from the kingdom of Israel

11.title: Do not fight
11.text: The prophet Shemaiah told Rehoboam not to go up to war against his brethren of Israel, for that division came from God — and the people obeyed and returned home.

11.question: Why did Rehoboam give up fighting against Israel?
options: Because the word of the Lord, by Shemaiah, forbade it
Because the priests interceded for peace between the brothers
Because Jeroboam promised to pay annual tribute to Judah
For fear of an alliance between Israel and Egypt

11.question: What did Rehoboam do to defend the kingdom of Judah?
options: He fortified cities and stocked them with provisions
Sent ambassadors to negotiate with Jeroboam
Formed a military alliance with the king of Egypt
Signed a peace treaty with Israel

11.question: What worship did Jeroboam set up in the north, driving the Levites to flee?
options: Worship of calves and goats (idols)
The restoration of worship at the temple of Jerusalem
The establishment of a priesthood according to the order of Levi
The practice of sacrifices to the god Moloch

11.question: Who moved to Judah, strengthening Rehoboam's kingdom?
options: The priests, Levites, and God-fearing of Israel
Merchants and craftsmen seeking wealth in Judah
The princes and nobles of Israel who supported Jeroboam
The mercenary warriors hired by Rehoboam

11.question: How did Rehoboam act wisely regarding his many sons?
options: He dispersed them through the fortified cities of Judah
He appointed them as priests responsible for the cities of Judah
He married them to the daughters of neighboring rulers
He sent them as ambassadors to the kingdom of Israel

12.title: When they humbled themselves
12.text: Seeing that the king and princes humbled themselves, the Lord told Shemaiah he would not utterly destroy them but grant some deliverance — though they would still serve Egypt.

12.question: Why did Shishak of Egypt come up against Judah?
options: Because Rehoboam and the people forsook the law of the Lord
Because Rehoboam refused to pay tribute to Egypt
Because Jeroboam asked Egypt for military aid against Judah
Because of an old dispute over borders

12.question: What did Shishak take when he plundered Jerusalem?
options: The temple and palace treasures, and the golden shields
The royal jewels and the sacred silver vessels of the temple
The horses and war chariots of Judah's entire army
The genealogical records kept in the royal archive

12.question: How did Rehoboam's reign end?
options: He died and his son Abijah reigned in his place
He was deposed by the princes and replaced by Abijah
He reigned twenty more years and was buried in Israel
He fled to Egypt, where he died in exile

13.title: God is with us
13.text: Abijah cried to Israel: 'Behold, God himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Israel, fight ye not against the Lord God of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper.'

13.question: What did Abijah proclaim on Mount Zemaraim?
options: That the kingdom of David was given by a covenant of salt to his sons
That the kingdom of Israel was given to Jeroboam by an eternal promise
That the priests of Israel would be accepted as legitimate by the Lord
That Judah would be delivered into Jeroboam's hand forever

13.question: What worship did Abijah accuse Israel of following?
options: The golden calves Jeroboam had made for gods
The silver images raised on the high places
The altars the kings of Israel built
The idol poles set up in Samaria

13.question: How did Jeroboam try to surprise Judah's army?
options: He set an ambush behind them
He sent false messengers to deceive Judah's leaders
He split his army into two wings to surround them
He hid troops in nearby hills

13.question: Why did Judah prevail over Israel?
options: Because they relied on the Lord God of their fathers
Because they had cavalry from foreign lands
Because they counted on support from other kingdoms
Because they held the strategic valley position

13.question: Where were Abijah's acts written?
options: In the commentary of the prophet Iddo
In the annals of the kingdom of Judah and Israel
In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
In the record of the priest Zadok

14.title: It is nothing for thee
14.text: Asa cried: 'Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power; help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on thee.' And the Lord struck the Ethiopians.

14.question: What did Asa command Judah to do at the start of his reign?
options: To seek the Lord and keep the law and commandment
To fortify all the cities and raise up a great army
To restore the high places and the old altars again
To make alliances with the neighboring kingdoms

14.question: Who came against Asa with an army of a million men?
options: Zerah the Ethiopian
Shishak of Egypt
Jeroboam
The Philistines

14.question: What happened to the Ethiopians before Judah?
options: They were struck and could not recover
They retreated in order and returned stronger
They made a lasting peace agreement with Asa
They withdrew without fighting against Judah

15.title: If ye seek him
15.text: Azariah said to Asa: 'The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.'

15.question: What happened to Israel when, in distress, they turned to the Lord?
options: He let himself be found by them
He pushed them even further away from him
He sent another prophet to judge them
He increased their afflictions

15.question: What did Asa do with the altar of the Lord?
options: He renewed it, before the porch of the temple
He replaced it entirely with an altar of pure silver
He moved it to the top of the sacred mountain
He decorated it with precious stones

15.question: How did the people seal the covenant to seek God?
options: They swore to the Lord with shouting, trumpets, and cornets
They raised a great altar of stones before all the assembled people
They signed a written pact before the royal seal of the king
They offered only silent prayers at the great temple

15.question: What marked the early years of Asa's reign after the reform?
options: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year
There was a brief peace followed by a new invasion
There was severe famine across all the territory of Judah
There were constant rebellions among the people

16.title: The eyes of the Lord
16.text: Hanani said to Asa: 'The eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly; therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.'

16.question: In whom did Asa trust against Baasha of Israel?
options: In Ben-hadad, king of Syria
In Baasha, king of Israel
In the Cushites and Libya
In Azariah the prophet

16.question: Why did Hanani rebuke Asa?
options: Because he leaned on Syria and not on the Lord
Because he offered impure sacrifices in the temple
Because he despised the counsel of the priests
Because he imprisoned the prophets of the Lord

16.question: What did Asa do when severely diseased in his feet?
options: He sought the physicians, and not the Lord
Gathered the priests, but did not trust them
Called the princes of Judah together for counsel
Offered sacrifices in the temple

17.title: Teaching the law
17.text: Jehoshaphat sent Levites and priests who went through all the cities of Judah carrying the book of the law of the Lord, teaching the people — a distinctive mark of his reign.

17.question: Why was the Lord with Jehoshaphat at first?
options: Because he walked in the first ways of David and sought not the Baalim
Because he conquered many fortified cities and greatly enriched the kingdom
Because he made alliances with neighboring kings to secure military protection
Because he offered great sacrifices in the temple at Jerusalem

17.question: What effect did Jehoshaphat's faithful reign have on neighboring kingdoms?
options: The fear of the Lord fell on them, and they made no war
They sent large armies to attack the fortified borders of Judah
They formed a strong military alliance against the kingdom of Judah
They sent ambassadors demanding greater tribute payments

17.question: What characterized Jehoshaphat's army?
options: It was numerous and organized under mighty captains
It was small, but formed entirely of specially chosen warriors
It was composed mainly of hired foreign mercenaries
It was organized only by untrained volunteers

17.question: Who served the king besides those set in the fortified cities?
options: Men of war stationed in Jerusalem
Singers appointed in the temple
Scribes who recorded the laws
Guards sent to the borders

18.title: What my God saith
18.text: Pressed to prophesy in Ahab's favor, Micaiah answered: 'As the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak' — and announced defeat, though it cost him prison.

18.question: What did Ahab's prophets say about the war for Ramoth-gilead?
options: To go up, for God would deliver it into the king's hand
That he should not go up, for the Syrians would surely defeat him
That he send envoys to negotiate peace with the Syrians
That he first consult the priests of Baal

18.question: What sign did Zedekiah make to promise Ahab victory?
options: Iron horns, saying with them he would push Syria
A bronze crown, saying with it he would reign over Syria
A broken spear, saying with it he would wound the king of Syria
A torn robe cut into twelve pieces, symbolizing victory

18.question: What did Micaiah finally prophesy to Ahab?
options: The defeat of Israel and the death of the king
The certain victory of Israel over Syria
A long and lasting peace between Israel and Syria
The conversion of King Ahab to the Lord

18.question: What vision did Micaiah report of the heavenly court?
options: A spirit that would deceive Ahab through the prophets' mouths
An angel with a fiery sword blocking the road to Ramoth-gilead
A scale weighing Ahab's good and evil deeds before the throne
A sealed book with the names of the false prophets

18.question: What did Micaiah tell Zedekiah, who had struck him?
options: That he would see the truth the day he hid in a chamber
That he would be greatly rewarded once the war had ended
That the Syrians would be utterly defeated before day's end
That King Ahab would return from war in peace and glory

18.question: How did Ahab enter battle to escape the prophecy?
options: In disguise, while Jehoshaphat wore royal robes
In royal robes, while Jehoshaphat wore a disguise
Mounted on a white horse at the front of the army
Hidden away deep inside the Syrian camp

18.question: How did Ahab die, fulfilling Micaiah's prophecy?
options: Struck by an arrow shot at random
Struck by the sword of a Syrian soldier
Hit by a stone thrown from the city wall
Killed in direct combat with the king of Syria

19.title: Ye judge for the Lord
19.text: Jehoshaphat said to the judges: 'Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.'

19.question: Why did the seer Jehu rebuke Jehoshaphat?
options: For helping wicked Ahab and loving those who hate the Lord
For permitting improper sacrifices at the high places of Judah
For appointing wicked priests to serve in the Lord's temple
For failing to destroy the altars of Baal in Judah

19.question: What did Jehoshaphat charge the judges he appointed?
options: To act faithfully and with a perfect heart, in the fear of the Lord
That they should consult the prophets before any decision
That they should judge according to local customs of each city
That they should impose heavy fines on offenders of every crime

20.title: Our eyes are upon thee
20.text: Jehoshaphat prayed before all Judah: 'O our God... we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.'

20.question: What did Jehoshaphat do on learning of the great multitude coming against Judah?
options: He feared, sought the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout Judah
He gathered the army and marched out to face the enemy without delay
He summoned the priests and offered sacrifices at the holy temple grounds
He sent messengers to seek help from the neighboring kings

20.question: What did Jehoshaphat remind God of in his prayer?
options: That these peoples came to drive Judah from the inheritance God gave them
That God had promised him victory over all the kings of the promised land
That the priests had sinned and brought divine wrath on all the people of Judah
Of the promise that his children would reign forever over Judah

20.question: What did the Levite Jahaziel announce to the people?
options: That the battle was not theirs, but God's
To gather the army in the valley to attack at dawn
To offer sacrifices before entering into battle
To send spies to observe the enemy camp

20.question: What did Jehoshaphat place before the army?
options: Singers to praise the beauty of holiness
War chariots covered with well-polished bronze
Priests sounding trumpets of silver before the people
Warriors armed with shields and spears

20.question: What did the people do on the fourth day, after the victory?
options: They gathered in the valley of Berachah to bless the Lord
Divided the spoils equally among the soldiers and the priests
Built a new altar in the temple to celebrate the great victory
Returned to the cities to rebuild the broken walls

20.question: How was Jehoshaphat's reign assessed?
options: He walked in the way of Asa, doing right in the Lord's eyes
He walked in the way of Omri, doing evil in the Lord's eyes
He did not follow his father's ways, but did evil in the Lord's eyes
He was compared to King Ahab, doing evil before the Lord

20.question: Why were Jehoshaphat's ships broken?
options: For having allied with Ahaziah, the wicked king of Israel
For having been built with wood that had rotted in storage
By a curse pronounced against them by the priests of Baal
For sailing across an excessively stormy and dangerous sea

21.title: For David's sake
21.text: Despite Jehoram's wickedness, the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with David, promising to give him and his sons a light forever.

21.question: What did Jehoram do when established in the kingdom?
options: He killed all his brothers with the sword
He made an alliance with the king of Edom against Judah
He rebuilt the idolatrous high places throughout the land
He appointed foreign priests in the temple

21.question: What happened with Edom in Jehoram's reign?
options: It rebelled and Judah lost dominion over it
It was subdued again and forced to pay heavy tribute
It received a new king appointed directly by Jehoram
It remained loyal to Judah throughout the war

21.question: What did Elijah's letter announce to Jehoram?
options: A great plague on the people and disease in his bowels
A long reign of great prosperity and peace for all his people
The complete restoration of the temple and purification of the priests
The total defeat of the Philistines and Arabians by his army

21.question: How did Jehoram die and was he buried?
options: Of a bowel disease, undesired and without a king's honors
In combat against the Philistines, mourned by all the people
In peace in his old age, with all the honors of a great king
Assassinated by conspirators within his own palace

22.title: The hidden child
22.text: Jehoshabeath hid the baby Joash, son of Ahaziah, from among the king's sons who were to be slain, keeping him in the temple for six years — so the house of David was not wiped out under Athaliah.

22.question: Who counseled Ahaziah to act wickedly?
options: His mother Athaliah, of Ahab's house
The high priest of the house of the Lord
The princes of Judah, his own brothers
The prophets of Baal in Samaria

22.question: What did Athaliah do on learning of her son Ahaziah's death?
options: She destroyed all the royal seed of Judah to reign
Gathered the priests to consecrate a new altar
Sent messengers to form an alliance with Syria
Wept and fasted before all the people of Judah

23.title: God save the king!
23.text: Jehoiada and his sons brought out the king's son, put the crown and the testimony on him, anointed him, and shouted: 'God save the king!' — restoring David's line to the throne.

23.question: Whom did Jehoiada gather to crown Joash safely?
options: The Levites, priests, and heads of the fathers' houses
The army captains and the nobles of the royal court of Judah
The elders of the tribes and the guards of the royal palace
The merchants and craftsmen of all Jerusalem

23.question: How did the people react on seeing the king crowned?
options: They rejoiced and blew trumpets; Athaliah cried 'Treason!'
They wept bitterly and fled to hide in the inner holy temple
They stayed in complete silence and refused to accept the new king
They stoned the Levites who guarded the temple gates

23.question: What covenant did Jehoiada make after crowning Joash?
options: That he, the people, and the king would be the Lord's people
An alliance with Syria to protect the newly anointed young king
An alliance with Israel to rebuild the great temple of Baal worship
An alliance with Egypt for free trade and mutual defense

23.question: What happened to the city after Athaliah's death?
options: It rejoiced and was quiet
It went into mourning for the queen's death
It came under siege from neighboring armies
It paid a heavy tribute

24.title: The Lord look on it
24.text: As he was stoned by Joash's order, Zechariah son of Jehoiada said as he died: 'The Lord look upon it, and require it' — the king had forgotten the good Jehoiada had done him.

24.question: What did Joash resolve to do to the temple?
options: Repair (restore) it
Enlarge it with new chambers
Replace it with a new altar
Consecrate it anew

24.question: How was the money for the work gathered?
options: In a chest set at the gate of the house of the Lord
Through contributions collected diligently house by house
By selling golden vessels from the old ruined temple
Charged upon the people as a mandatory royal tax

24.question: What happened while Jehoiada lived?
options: Burnt offerings were made continually in the house of the Lord
There was constant idolatry spread throughout all the land of Judah
The temple stood closed and abandoned for many very long years
There was continual war against the Philistines and Ammonites

24.question: What did God send to bring Judah back to him?
options: Prophets, but the people would not hear them
A foreign army sent to punish the wicked king
A very severe drought over all the land of Judah
An angel sent to warn them directly

24.question: What did Syria's army do to Judah at the end of Joash's reign?
options: It struck Judah and Joash, destroying the princes
It made an alliance with Judah against invading Assyrians
It withdrew without fighting before all of Judah's army
It paid heavy tribute directly to King Joash

24.question: How did Joash die?
options: His own servants slew him, for the blood of Zechariah
He died in battle against the Syrians, wounded badly in both legs
He died of a grave illness after many years of prosperous reign
He died in peace, buried with honor among the kings of Judah

25.title: The Lord can give more
25.text: When Amaziah lamented the hundred talents paid to the mercenaries he had dismissed, the man of God said: 'The Lord is able to give thee much more than this' — for victory comes from God, not money.

25.question: What principle of the law did Amaziah follow in punishing his father's killers?
options: That fathers not die for children, nor children for fathers
That fathers answer for the sins of their children to the third generation
That the whole family of the offender be punished together with him
That the king has power to pardon any crime committed

25.question: Why did Amaziah dismiss the mercenaries of Israel?
options: A man of God warned the Lord was not with them
A prophet said they would bring a curse on Judah's army
The priests declared they were unclean for holy war
They refused to return plunder taken from Edom

25.question: What sin did Amaziah commit after defeating Edom?
options: He brought back Edom's gods and worshiped them
He made an alliance with Moab against Judah
He worshiped the old idols of Judah
He rebuilt the temple of Baal

25.question: Why did Amaziah not heed Joash's warning against war?
options: Because it was from God, to deliver them for seeking Edom's gods
Because he trusted the strength of his army and Jerusalem's defenses
Because the priests had prophesied certain victory over the king of Israel
Because he wished to avenge his father's earlier defeat

25.question: What did Joash take from Jerusalem after defeating Amaziah?
options: Gold, silver, temple vessels, and hostages
The tablets of the law and the golden candlestick of the temple
The sacred vessels of the altar and the priestly garments
The jewels, the crown, and the royal scepter of Judah

25.question: How did Amaziah's reign end?
options: He was slain in a conspiracy and buried in Jerusalem
He fled to Egypt and there died, never returning to Judah
He reigned to old age and died peacefully in his own bed
He was deposed by the people and exiled forever

26.title: When he was strong
26.text: 'But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar' — a task reserved for the priests.

26.question: What happened while Uzziah sought the Lord?
options: God made him prosper
He lost every battle
The people rebelled against him
Uzziah fell gravely ill

26.question: What shows that Uzziah loved farming?
options: He dug wells and had farmers and vinedressers
He distributed fertile lands among priests and Levites
He built granaries and storehouses in every city
He imported wheat and wine from other nations

26.question: How did Uzziah equip his army?
options: With shields, spears, helmets, breastplates, bows, and slings
With swords, axes, battering rams, torches, and heavy war ropes
By hiring foreign mercenaries armed only with spears and shields
Only with simple wooden bows and arrows of no strength

26.question: Why did the priests resist Uzziah in the temple?
options: Because only the priests could burn incense to the Lord
Because the king had forbidden any sacrifice in the temple
Because the prophet Zechariah had ordered no one to enter
Because they feared the people's anger against the king

26.question: How did Uzziah end his days?
options: A leper and isolated, buried apart from the kings
He received full pardon and reigned peacefully some years more
He was slain in battle and buried with honor among the kings
He fled into the desert and disappeared forever

27.title: He ordered his ways
27.text: 'So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God' — the secret of his power was not military, but faithfulness.

27.question: How did Jotham differ from his father Uzziah?
options: He did not enter the temple of the Lord
He entered the temple and offered incense himself
He was struck with leprosy and died in isolation
He became corrupted along with all the people

27.question: Why did Jotham become mighty?
options: Because he ordered his ways before the Lord
Because he received great yearly tribute from the kings of Syria
Because he formed a military alliance with the kings of Israel
Because he defeated the armies of Egypt in battle

28.title: In distress, he sinned more
28.text: 'In the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord: this is that king Ahaz' — instead of humbling himself, he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had struck him.

28.question: What abomination did Ahaz commit, copying the pagans?
options: He burned his children in the fire
He sacrificed his children to Egyptian idols
He built a pagan temple inside Jerusalem
He desecrated the sacred vessels of the temple

28.question: What did the prophet Oded demand of Israel concerning Judah's captives?
options: That they return them, for they too were guilty before God
That they release them, but keep all the plundered goods for themselves
That they keep them imprisoned as permanent slaves in Samaria
That they hand them over to the priests for sacrifice

28.question: What did the men of Israel do with Judah's captives?
options: They clothed, fed, and brought the feeble back to Jericho
They whipped them, took their clothes, and drove them out of Samaria
They divided the spoil among themselves and kept the captives imprisoned
They took them as slaves to the lands of Ephraim

28.question: What did Assyria do for Ahaz, who had called it?
options: Instead of helping, it distressed him
It sent troops to defend its borders
It made an eternal covenant of peace with Judah
It returned all the tribute paid

28.question: How was Ahaz buried?
options: In the city, but not in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel
With great pomp and honor beside his illustrious royal ancestors
In the royal sepulchres of Jerusalem, beside Uzziah his grandfather
Outside the walls of Jerusalem, in a foreign land

29.title: Opening the doors
29.text: In the very first month of his first year, Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the Lord, which Ahaz had shut, and repaired them — restoring the interrupted worship.

29.question: How did Hezekiah describe the fathers' sin to the Levites?
options: That they forsook the Lord and turned their backs on his tabernacle
That they offered sacrifices to foreign gods in the sanctuary of the Lord
That they allied with neighboring kings and abandoned the law of Moses forever
That they neglected the daily sacrifices on the holy altar

29.question: What did Hezekiah purpose in his heart to do?
options: Make a covenant with the Lord, to turn away God's fierce wrath
Build a new defensive wall to protect Jerusalem from its enemies
Restore trade with neighboring kingdoms to strengthen the treasury
Send messengers to ask the king of Assyria for help

29.question: What did the priests and Levites do with the temple's uncleanness?
options: They carried it out to the brook Kidron
They buried it secretly in the temple's inner court
They burned it completely before the main altar
They kept it for future offerings

29.question: What was offered in the cleansing of the temple and kingdom?
options: Burnt offerings and a sin offering for Judah
Grain offerings and drink offerings for all the people of Israel
Firstfruits and tithes brought by the priests and Levites
Only incense burned on the golden altar

29.question: How did Hezekiah arrange the music in worship?
options: With Levites, cymbals, psalteries, and harps, by David's order
With priests, trumpets and drums, after the custom of the Egyptians
With pagan musicians, drums and flutes, against the order of Moses
With only silent chants, without any instrument at all

29.question: How did the people respond to the restoration of worship?
options: They brought many burnt offerings with joy
They refused to take part in the offerings presented
They complained about the taxes collected for the temple
They remained indifferent to the religious ceremonies

29.question: Why did Hezekiah and the people rejoice?
options: Because God had prepared the people, for it was done suddenly
Because they defeated the neighboring armies without losing a soldier
Because they received great riches from the neighboring foreign kingdoms
Because they made a lasting peace treaty with Assyria

30.title: Turn again unto him
30.text: Hezekiah's invitation said: 'turn again unto the Lord... for the Lord your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.'

30.question: What feast did Hezekiah invite all Israel to keep in Jerusalem?
options: The Passover of the Lord
The feast of harvest
The Day of Atonement
The feast of tabernacles

30.question: How did many in the north react to Hezekiah's messengers?
options: They laughed and mocked them
They accepted the invitation with great enthusiasm
They attacked the king's messengers with stones
They ignored them completely

30.question: What did the gathered people do before the Passover?
options: They removed the altars in Jerusalem and cast them into the Kidron
They rebuilt the old altars in order to worship many other foreign gods
They offered sacrifices on the many pagan altars throughout Jerusalem
They consulted the priests of Baal before the great feast

30.question: Why did Hezekiah pray for those who ate the Passover unclean?
options: That God pardon everyone who prepared his heart to seek him
That the priests would receive greater honor before the people
That Hezekiah would always be recognized as the greatest king of Judah
To postpone the feast until the following whole year

30.question: What did the assembly decide after the seven days of feast?
options: To keep another seven days with joy
To return immediately to their homes and cities
To fast for seven days as a sign of repentance
To offer human sacrifices to the Lord

30.question: What did the priests and Levites do at the feast's end?
options: They blessed the people, and their prayer reached heaven
They collected a special tribute from all the assembled people
They dismissed the people in silence, without any blessing
They closed the temple until the next great feast

31.title: With all his heart
31.text: 'And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered' — the summary of Hezekiah's reign.

31.question: What did the people bring in abundance when Hezekiah gave the command?
options: The firstfruits and tithes of everything
Only gold and silver from the royal houses
Only priestly garments and weapons of war
Only coins of silver and gold

31.question: What did the high priest say about the heaped-up offerings?
options: That they ate, were satisfied, and plenty was left over
That everything was lacking and the people suffered hunger for many months
That the offerings were completely destroyed by fire before arriving
That the priests complained of great food shortage

31.question: Why did the priests and Levites receive their portion?
options: So they might devote themselves to the service of the Lord's house
So that they might become powerful military leaders within the kingdom
So that they might build large and comfortable houses for themselves
To provide support for the royal army stationed near the king

31.question: Why did Hezekiah prosper in all things?
options: Because he did everything with all his heart, seeking his God
Because he made a secret alliance with the king of Egypt
Because he received riches from foreign merchants
Because he followed the counsel of ancient false prophets

32.title: With us is the Lord
32.text: Hezekiah encouraged the people: 'With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles' — and the people rested on these words.

32.question: What did Hezekiah do to weaken the Assyrian siege?
options: He stopped the water springs outside the city
He opened the river gates against the enemy
He tore down the walls to deceive Sennacherib
He sent spies to the Assyrian camp

32.question: How did Sennacherib try to dishearten Judah?
options: He mocked, saying no god had saved its people from Assyria
He promised great riches and lands to those who surrendered without a fight
He sent messengers offering peace in exchange for yearly tribute
He publicly praised Hezekiah's faith before the people

32.question: Against whom did Sennacherib's servants speak blasphemies?
options: Against the Lord God and against Hezekiah
Against the prophets and against the people of Judah
Against the priests and against the Levites
Against the king of Assyria and his servants

32.question: What happened after the angel of the Lord struck the Assyrians?
options: Many brought gifts to the Lord and to Hezekiah
Many fled to Egypt in fear of the war
Many rebelled against the reign of Hezekiah
Many demanded tribute from the defeated Assyrians

32.question: How did Hezekiah respond, in the end, to the pride of his heart?
options: He humbled himself, with Jerusalem, and wrath did not come in his days
He persisted in pride and refused to acknowledge his fault before the people
He was dethroned by the princes of Judah because of his excessive pride
He worshiped foreign idols together with the people of Jerusalem

32.question: How was Hezekiah buried?
options: With honors, in the chief of the sepulchres of the sons of David
Without any honors, far from the city, because of his earlier pride
Outside the city of David, in a common grave, without any ceremony
In Babylon, far away from his native land, as a prisoner

33.title: And he humbled himself
33.text: Imprisoned in Babylon, Manasseh prayed and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers; God was entreated, heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem — 'then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.'

33.question: Where did Manasseh dare to build altars to other gods?
options: In the two courts of the house of the Lord
On the roof of the royal palace in Jerusalem
In the high places of all the cities of Judah
Beside the gates of the city of David

33.question: How did Manasseh and the people respond to the Lord's warning?
options: They would not listen
They repented at once
They reformed the temple
They fled

33.question: What did Manasseh do after returning repentant from Babylon?
options: He repaired the Lord's altar and commanded Judah to serve the Lord
He rebuilt the idolatrous altars and resumed pagan sacrifices
He summoned all the priests to rebuild the temple from scratch
He appointed his son Amon as high priest of the temple

33.question: Who reigned after Manasseh's death?
options: His son Amon
His nephew
A prophet
A priest

33.question: How did Amon's short reign end?
options: The people of the land slew the conspirators and made Josiah king
The conspirators seized the throne and reigned for many years
The Assyrian army invaded Judah and exiled the whole royal family
The priests gathered and anointed Amon again as king

34.title: He tore his clothes
34.text: When he heard the words of the Book of the Law found in the temple, Josiah tore his clothes, for he saw how great was God's wrath because his fathers had not kept the word of the Lord.

34.question: What did Josiah do to the bones of the idolatrous priests?
options: He burned them on their altars, cleansing Judah
He buried them in the valley of Ben-Hinnom, far from the city
He took them to Jerusalem and displayed them before the people
He threw them into the waters of the brook Kidron

34.question: What was the money gathered in the temple used for?
options: To pay the workers who repaired the house of the Lord
To buy priestly garments for the high priest to wear
To finance the war against the mighty king of Assyria
To buy animals for the sacrifices at the temple

34.question: What did Hilkiah the priest find in the temple?
options: The Book of the Law of the Lord, given by Moses
A scroll with prophecies of Isaiah about Judah
A collection of psalms written by King David
A genealogical record of the priests

34.question: Why did Josiah send to inquire of the Lord about the Book?
options: Because great was God's wrath, for the fathers had not kept the word
Because he wanted to confirm whether the book was truly ancient and authentic
Because Hilkiah insisted it was necessary for the temple's records
Because he feared the Assyrians had written the book

34.question: Why did Huldah say Josiah would be spared the judgment?
options: Because his heart was tender and he humbled himself before God
Because he had rebuilt all the temples destroyed by the Assyrians
Because he offered great sacrifices of gold and silver at the Lord's temple
Because he was a direct descendant of the pious king Hezekiah

34.question: What did Josiah do after renewing the covenant?
options: He removed the abominations from all Israel's lands and made the people serve the Lord
He appointed new idolatrous priests to serve at the pagan altars throughout the land of Judah
He rebuilt the pagan temples that had been destroyed by the former kings of ancient Judah
He sent messengers to gather all the people into the city of Jerusalem

35.title: None since Samuel
35.text: 'There was no passover like to that kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet' — Josiah's Passover surpassed in faithfulness all those of the kings before him.

35.question: How did Josiah organize the Levites for the Passover?
options: By courses, according to the fathers' houses, as David had written
By lineage, according to the ancient custom of the priests of Aaron
By lot, according to the tradition established by the princes of Israel
By order of birth, according to ancient royal custom

35.question: What was prepared for the keeping of the Passover?
options: The service, with priests and Levites in their places
The royal army, gathered to protect the temple and the holy city
Only the sacred vessels, still kept in the treasury
Only the singers, still without the other Levites

35.question: Who sang while the Passover was offered?
options: The singers, the sons of Asaph, in their place
The Egyptian priests, brought by Necho for the feast
The women of Jerusalem, gathered beside the altar
The princes of Judah, before the people

35.question: What warning did Necho give Josiah before the battle?
options: That God had sent him, and Josiah should not oppose God
That the gods of Egypt would protect him against any army
That Josiah should ally with him against Assyria
That he should return to Jerusalem without fighting

35.question: How did Josiah die?
options: Wounded by arrows in battle against Necho, at Megiddo
Poisoned by a treacherous adviser during a royal banquet in Jerusalem
Killed by a sudden fever after returning from a long journey to Jerusalem
Captured and executed by Egyptian soldiers at Megiddo

36.title: The land enjoyed her sabbaths
36.text: The exile lasted seventy years, 'to fulfil the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths' — resting all the time of the desolation.

36.question: What was Jehoiakim's reign in Judah like?
options: He did evil in the eyes of the Lord
He did what was right before the people
He ruled with justice and fear of God
He was faithful to the commandments

36.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar take when he exiled Jehoiachin?
options: Jehoiachin and the precious vessels of the house of the Lord
The temple treasures and the sons of the princes of Judah as hostages
All the chief priests and the sacred garments of the high priest
Only the official records and documents of the kingdom of Judah

36.question: Why did the Lord send his messengers to Judah?
options: Because he had compassion on his people and his dwelling place
Because he wanted to test the faithfulness of the priests and prophets of Judah
Because he desired to establish a new covenant with the neighboring kings of Judah
Because he wanted to test his prophets one more time

36.question: What did the Babylonians do to Jerusalem?
options: They burned God's house, broke down the wall, and destroyed its palaces
They fortified the city, restored the temple, and appointed new priests
They distributed grain to the people, repaired the wall, and built new altars
They took only the gold vessels, without touching the buildings

36.question: What did Cyrus, king of Persia, decree at the end of the book?
options: That the house of the Lord be rebuilt in Jerusalem and the people go up
That all the Jews should remain exiled in Babylon for another seventy years
That a new pagan temple should be built in honor of all the gods of ancient Persia
That the priests be executed for their disobedience to the king
